exposure: supraumbilical laparotomy and fundal transverse CS
standard CS (suprapubic Joel-Cohen laparotomy and lower uterine segment transverse incision)
cohort: The study included 55 women aged 29-41 years with singleton pregnancies and morbid obesity (BMI > 40 kg/m2), primarily older primiparous women, with comorbidities such as cardiovascular diseases and endocrine pathology, who underwent cesarean section.
finding: Supraumbilical laparotomy with fundal transverse CS demonstrated advantages over standard CS in pregnant women with morbid obesity, including reduced intraoperative blood loss, shorter fetal extraction time and CS duration, decreased postoperative pain, shorter hospital stay, and a lower risk of surgical wound and uterine complications.
